AccountLink.description:
De standen die iets DOEN.

Hier stond ook ``VERIFY``, en die deed niets: ``keycloak_yaml_handler`` bouwt alleen
voor ``automatic`` en ``confirm`` een eigen first-broker-login-flow en laat de rest op
Keycloaks eigen flow staan - precies wat je krijgt als je niets kiest. Wie ``verify``
koos kreeg dus dezelfde uitkomst als wie het veld leeg liet, terwijl de keuzelijst
deed alsof er een verschil was.
AccountLink.title: AccountLink

KeycloakClientEntry.description:
An ``additional-clients`` item. Only ``name`` is guardrailed; the rest
(redirect-uris, ...) is advanced pass-through -- the hard 10% the plan leaves
hand-authored -- so extras are allowed.

name.description: Client id of the extra client to create in the realm.
name.title: Name

KeycloakClientEntry.title: KeycloakClientEntry

KeycloakRealm.description:
Per-realm admin connection (OPI-managed, one per cluster).

Relocated verbatim from the old project-level ``config.keycloak`` (RC-5 B). Kept
as-is -- matched by ``realm`` (deterministic ``{project}-{cluster}``) as before.
``extra="allow"`` tolerates fields written over time (e.g. ``service_client_secret``);
password is stored AGE-encrypted or ``plain:``-prefixed, so it's just a string here.

host.description: Keycloak base URL this realm lives on. Written by the platform.
host.title: Host

realm.description: Realm name, {project}-{cluster}. Written by the platform.
realm.title: Realm

totp_secret.description: Shared TOTP seed for the realm-admin account, stored like the password. Only present when the cluster provisions admin OTP.
totp_secret.title: Totp Secret

username.description: Realm-admin account the platform manages the realm with.
username.title: Username

KeycloakRealm.title: KeycloakRealm

KeycloakRealmRoleEntry.description: A ``realm-roles`` item; ``name`` required, advanced keys pass through.

name.description: Name of the realm role to create.
name.title: Name

KeycloakRealmRoleEntry.title: KeycloakRealmRoleEntry

RestrictAccessConfig.description: ``restrict-access`` sub-object; keys are well-defined so extras are forbidden.

enabled.description: Whether sign-in is limited to users holding the role below.
enabled.title: Enabled

error-message.description: Message shown to a user without the role; a ${...} value is a Keycloak message key.
error-message.title: Error-Message

realm-role.description: Realm role a user must hold to be let in.
realm-role.title: Realm-Role

role.description: Client role a user must hold to be let in.
role.title: Role

RestrictAccessConfig.title: RestrictAccessConfig

account-link.description: How an existing account is linked when a user signs in through an identity provider: automatic or confirm. Leave it out for Keycloak's own flow (verification by email).

additional-clients.description: Extra Keycloak clients to create in the realm.
additional-clients.title: Additional-Clients

additional_redirect_uris.description: Extra redirect URIs the client accepts, on top of the deployment URLs (e.g. localhost for development).
additional_redirect_uris.title: Additional Redirect Uris

realms.description: Per-cluster realm admin connections. Written and managed by the platform: it is carried over on a write, so a caller neither has to send it nor can lose it by leaving it out.
realms.title: Realms

restrict-access.description: Limit sign-in to users holding a given role.

template.description: Realm template the realm is created from; 'sso-only' is single sign-on without extras.

variables.description: Values filled into the realm template's placeholders.
